class.name: GameStateBase
class.brief_description: What everyone is allowed to know about the match.
class.description: Created by the [World] rather than by the game mode, because the game mode is the server's alone while this has to exist on clients too - that split is the whole reason the class is separate. It holds the [PlayerState] of every player, on every peer. [method get_server_world_time_seconds] gives the server's clock as this peer best knows it, so a timer started on the server reads the same everywhere. Extend it in GDScript for anything the whole match shares - the score, the round number, the objective - and return those property names from [code]_get_replicated_properties[/code] to have the framework keep them in step.

method.name: _get_replicated_properties
method.description: Override to add your own properties to what is kept in step across peers. Return their names; the framework attaches the synchronizer, so a project places no [MultiplayerSynchronizer] of its own.

method.name: _init_game_state
method.description: Override for setup that every peer needs - unlike a game mode's, this hook runs on clients too.

method.name: add_player_state
method.description: Reparents [param player_state] under this node and adds it to the list. The framework does this as players log in.

method.name: get_player_array
method.description: Every player in the match, as seen from this peer. This is what a scoreboard reads - it lists players at other machines too, which is exactly why player data lives here and not on the controller.

method.name: get_player_count
method.description: How many players are in the match.

method.name: get_player_state_by_index
method.description: The player at [param player_index] in the list, or null.

method.name: get_player_state_by_player_id
method.description: The player with the server-assigned [param player_id], or null.

method.name: get_player_state_by_unique_id
method.description: The players on connection [param unique_id]. The server is [constant World.SERVER_PEER_ID], which is also what a game with no peer reports.

method.name: get_server_world_time_seconds
method.description: The server's clock as this peer best knows it: measured directly on the server, carried forward from the last update on a client. Use it for anything that has to mean the same thing on both sides.

method.name: get_world
method.description: The world this game state belongs to.

method.name: handle_begin_play
method.description: Marks the match as running. The game mode calls this once the level is up and players may join.

method.name: has_authority
method.description: True on the server, and in a game with no peer at all.

method.name: remove_player_state
method.description: Takes a player out of the list, on logout.

members.member: Set once the game mode has started the level. Clients read it to know the match is really running rather than still being built.
The server's clock, so every peer can agree on when something happened. Read it through [method get_server_world_time_seconds], which carries it forward between updates on a client.

signal.name: begun_play
signal.description: The match started - [member has_begun_play] turned true. Fires on every peer, which is what makes it usable for client-side UI.
